evidence: The file's first line says it is GENERATED from the install.sh template and is reconverged on every run, so a hand edit here would be overwritten. The reviewer called the action 'arbitrary third-party', but it is in the same promptctl org; the mutable-tag risk the agent conceded ('a compromised org account retargets a mutable v1') is real, and the agent sent it to the template owner as miser-cicd-c2i.

The reviewer hedged its own claim ('I'm not fully certain'). The agent quoted GitHub's 2021-10-06 changelog: Dependabot pull_request runs 'will begin to respect the permissions specified in your workflows' and keep read-only defaults. That matches the comment as written, so applying the suggested correction would have made a true comment false.

The triggers include opened/synchronize/reopened with no draft guard, plus ready_for_review, so a draft PR is reviewed on every push and then reviewed again on the same SHA. The agent confirmed this, explained why cancel-in-progress does not cover the duplicate, and put the fix in the template ticket instead of the generated copy.

narrative: This PR installs a generated review workflow and had one review round. Two findings were real (a mutable action tag, duplicate draft reviews), but both belong in the install.sh template, so the agent routed them to a ticket instead of editing the derived copy. The third finding came from an outdated idea of how Dependabot token permissions work, and the agent refuted it with GitHub's changelog.
guidance_observations: The agent checked the generated-file header before acting and refused hand edits to derived output, which avoided drift the next installer run would have caused.
Answering a self-declared uncertain finding with a cited primary source closed it in one reply.

evidence: The new lastLineUsage doc said 'all 5,395 streaming groups', while the completeUsage doc added in the same diff re-measured that figure as 5,449 and called 5,395 stale. The fix in dcd16c0 updated only this one line, and the same stale figures survived elsewhere (F8, F9, F13).
guidance_note: When a PR re-measures a figure, grep the whole diff for the old value (5,395, 36,426, 'three groups') and replace every occurrence in the same commit, not just the one the reviewer pointed at.

evidence: For c.index === e.start, expected reduces to calls[e.start].usage.cacheRead, which is the call's own actual value, so these calls matched by construction and inflated exactCalls. The fix in d58e999 added a predictable flag, but it also changed callsChecked, the invariants basis figures, and a spawned-conversations assertion, and each of those drew a new finding (F5/F7, F6/F10, F17).
guidance_note: When changing a metric's denominator, trace every consumer of the old denominator (render's callsExact === callsChecked, tests asserting against calls.length, prose stating the old rate) and check the zero case and each restated number before pushing.

evidence: auditCorpus(scanned) was called in two tests over the same input. The b32471f diff hoists it into the describe body, and both tests now use the shared result.

generate.ts still listed 'the independent oracles over corpus-wide conservation (miser-pipeline-sll.6)' as STILL UNVERIFIED, but this PR adds exactly that oracle. The fix in 4fe4205 moved the item and listed the new tests.
guidance_note: When a PR closes a ticket that a self-verification checklist names, update that checklist in the same PR.

evidence: The F2 fix promised to 're-measure and update the affected basis comments (~84.6%)'. It updated invariants.ts to '83.7% of 41,067 PREDICTABLE calls' but left residency.ts at 84.6%, and since epoch-openers always match, the two figures cannot both hold. The replacement in daa0eab (84.2% all calls, 83.9% predictable, still over 47,782) was arithmetically inconsistent again (F14).
guidance_note: When restating two linked rates, recompute one from the other (all-calls = predictable rate times predictable share plus the opener share) before writing either down.

evidence: The project.ts diff changes callsChecked from calls.length to predictableCalls, and render's unchanged callsExact === callsChecked then shows the 'exact' ok badge for 0-of-0 on every single-call or all-opener session. The fix in 319b860 added a three-way status, but its narration for the empty case was wrong (F15) and it moved a doc comment (F22).
guidance_note: When a fix can drive a count to zero, find every equality or ratio over that count and decide what zero means there before pushing.

evidence: This duplicates F5 with different arithmetic: it reconstructs 86.0% from invariants.ts's 83.7%/41,067, which conflicts with residency.ts's 84.6%. The conflict comes from the F2 fix updating only one of the two places. It was resolved by the same daa0eab commit.
The test comment still said 'the 5,395 corpus groups', the same stale figure the F1 fix corrected only in calls.ts:36. The 74c9246 diff changes it to 5,449.
guidance_note: When fixing a stale figure, grep the repo for the old number and fix every hit in the same commit.

evidence: 'The three corpus groups whose final line is a placeholder' contradicts the PR's own re-measured '53 groups of the corpus's 48,155' in fixtures.ts. It is a different fact but the same staleness, which a sweep after F1 would have caught. The 74c9246 diff changes it to 53.
guidance_note: After any re-measurement, list every corpus count the PR states and check each one against the new scan, not only the count a reviewer flagged.

evidence: This duplicates F6: when predictableCalls is 0, render shows a green 'exact' badge for '0 of 0', which the reviewer correctly describes as the vacuous match relocated rather than removed. It was resolved by the same 319b860 commit.

The structural gap was real: claims mapped over every call, and a block with no breakdown produces 0 by construction. The predicted size of the inflation ('far more than 91,301') was wrong, because the agent found 'every call happens to carry a breakdown so the site count didn't change'. The ON-POST-REVIEW flag is a false positive: the unfiltered claims are original PR code that the b32471f hoist did not touch.
guidance_note: When an identity filters to applicable sites, check that every identity in the same table has its own applicability filter, not just the ones written first.

evidence: The base-term fix targets non-initial epochs, but the fixtures the reviewer cites each have a single epoch (resumed(), cold start, and a strictly increasing 0/1000/1500/2300). The flag is a false positive: these fixtures predate the b32471f commit, which touched only corpus-smoke. The agent added a two-epoch fixture in daa0eab.
guidance_note: When a fix targets a specific case (here, a second epoch after a cache_read drop), add a fixture that contains that case before relying on corpus scans.

evidence: buildTranscript's doc still said '5,395 of the corpus's 36,426 request groups', the same stale pair F1 corrected in calls.ts. The 74c9246 diff changes it to 5,449/48,155.
guidance_note: When fixing a stale figure, grep the repo for the old number and fix every hit in the same commit.

evidence: The figures the F5 fix wrote are inconsistent: (0.839 x 41,547 + 6,235) / 47,782 is about 86.0%, not the stated 84.2%. The agent conceded 'last round's fix conflated two different corpus scans' totals in one paragraph'. The named commit 74c9246 only touched test figures; the cause is daa0eab, F5's fix.
guidance_note: Before pushing re-measured percentages, check that every rate in the paragraph shares one denominator from the same scan, and recompute the derived rate from the stated counts.

evidence: The 'empty' narration added in 319b860 says 'Every call here opened its own epoch' whenever callsChecked === 0. A root conversation with zero calls (a shape spans.ts documents as real) also has callsChecked 0, so the page would make a false causal claim. The fix in 9538e0f added rootCalls.
guidance_note: When writing narration for a new status, list every input state that maps to that status and check that the sentence is true for each of them.

evidence: The template `00:01:${String(k).padStart(2,'0')}` produces '00:01:60' when k reaches 60. parseLine's `Date.parse(...) || 0` would turn that silently into ts 0. The bug is latent (callers pass 1-2 usages) but cheap to fix. The flag is a false positive: 74c9246 only edited a comment figure in fixtures.ts, and the packet does not show a review fix introducing usageBlockSession.
guidance_note: Build synthetic timestamps with Date arithmetic, as the existing at() helper does, instead of string templates that can overflow.

evidence: The F2 fix replaced `exactCalls toBe calls.length` (a concrete 4) with `exactCalls toBe predictableCalls`. That passes whenever every predictable call matches, including when a misclassification makes predictableCalls 0, so the test lost its power. The fix in 1b8ba94 pins 3.
guidance_note: When changing an assertion's expected value to another computed field, keep a concrete literal so the test cannot reduce to x === x.

evidence: For a single-line group, usage and lastLineUsage come from the same line, so agreement is trivial, and those groups were most of the 47,949 sites. Accepting was right, but the chosen filter (lineCount > 1) was still wrong and produced 35,102 sites against the PR's own 5,449 streaming figure (F21). The flag is a false positive: groupsWithRealLastLine is original PR code that 74c9246 did not touch.
guidance_note: When excluding vacuous sites, compare the new site count with the PR's own independent figure for that population (5,449 streaming groups) and treat a 6x gap as a wrong filter.

evidence: A tiny corpus could lack one identity's pattern. But the per-identity zero-site check was the only guard against a single identity silently certifying nothing, and the agent replaced it with 'total sites across all identities > 0' plus 'describeAudit still prints... for a human to notice', which reopens exactly that silent pass. The flag is a false positive: the test body is original, and the F3 hoist only moved where audits is computed.
guidance_note: Before weakening a no-silent-failure assertion to address an edge case, ask whether the weakened form still catches the regression the assertion was written for. If it does not, push back or scope the exemption narrowly.

evidence: '9,105,348 tokens — 27.4%' came from the same 740-transcript run whose group counts the PR flagged as stale. The 74c9246 stale-figure sweep (fixes for F8/F9/F13) did not cover these. The fix in 309977d labels them HISTORICAL, which is one of the two options the reviewer offered.
guidance_note: When a PR declares one scan's figures stale, mark or re-measure every figure from that scan in the same pass.

evidence: The F18 fix filtered on lineCount > 1 and recorded '35,102 (the genuinely multi-line/streaming groups)', while the same PR states 5,449 streaming groups. The agent then verified that most multi-line groups have constant output; the outputVaries filter in bbede82 gave 5,451 sites.
guidance_note: When a fix reports a measured count, reconcile it against every other figure the PR states for the same population before pushing.

evidence: The F15 hunk shows that residencyCheck's doc and function, added for F6 in 319b860, were inserted between arenaBasisCheck's doc comment and arenaBasisCheck itself. That left the arena comment sitting on the wrong function. The fix in fdf9f55 moved it back.
guidance_note: When inserting a new function, place it between declarations, not between an existing doc comment and the function it documents.

evidence: The four-way residencyCheck branching was written over two fixes (319b860, 9538e0f) to remove a vacuous badge, and no test exercised it. The reviewer notes that only portability.test.ts calls renderCorpus. The agent added render.test.ts in fcfd9bc.
guidance_note: A fix that adds branching logic ships with a test per branch in the same commit.

evidence: The F15 fix's no-calls copy asserts 'Every call here was delegated to a spawned agent' whenever rootCalls === 0, but Conservation carries no signal that any spawned work exists. The reviewer was unsure the shape occurs in real data, and the packet does not show whether it does; the overclaim in the code is real either way. The fix in 8a291ad added hasSpawnedWork.
guidance_note: When narration asserts a cause, check that the value deciding the branch actually encodes that cause and not just its absence.

narrative: The PR ran into the 5-round review cap. Most of the review cost came from the F2 fix (a predictable-call exclusion). It changed a denominator, a rendered status, prose percentages and a test assertion, and each of those drew a new finding, which branched into further rounds (0/0 badge, then false narration, then a delegation overclaim; inconsistent percentages twice; a tautological test). Fixes for stale figures were applied one instance at a time, so the same old numbers came back in later rounds. The F18 fix picked a filter whose site count (35,102) contradicted the PR's own 5,449 figure. Rounds 3 and 4 found nothing but fix-caused findings, and round 5 was the unreviewed cap round.
guidance_observations: The agent fixed each finding narrowly and pushed without tracing the fix's ripple through its consumers. One sweep per fix (consumers of the changed field, every restatement of a changed figure, the zero case) would have collapsed several rounds.
Numbers in prose were treated as text, not data. Recomputing derived rates from the stated counts before pushing would have caught F5, F14 and F21 locally.
The agent accepted every finding, including F19, where accepting removed a no-silent-failure guard; uniform acceptance under round pressure is a risk.

evidence: The test only iterates the root conversation plus forest.placed, and Orphan carries no conversation, so 'every real conversation on disk' overstated coverage. The 5f5eae4 diff rewords it to 'every ROOT or PLACED conversation' and notes that orphans are excluded.
guidance_note: When writing a coverage claim, read the loop it describes and state its actual domain.

evidence: assistantOutput is sized with exactSize(c.usage.output), so 'prices every cause with [the estimator]' was false. The 5f5eae4 fix narrowed the claim, but the rewritten sentence kept the original error that unattributed is exact, which led to F5.
guidance_note: When rewriting a sentence to fix one false claim, re-verify every other claim in that sentence against the code.

evidence: Cause collapsed Arrival.size (which carries its Basis) into a bare estTokens number, so the exact-vs-estimated tag that Size exists to carry was lost. The 5f5eae4 diff adds basis: Basis from a.size.basis and pins it in tests.
guidance_note: When aggregating values of a tagged type, carry the tag into the aggregate instead of dropping it to a bare number.

evidence: The test's call-1 case shows unattributed at -695, driven by the exact 1000-cost prior-output bucket against a 375 exact cost, not by chars/4 error. The 5f5eae4 diff now names both causes.
guidance_note: When documenting why a value can be negative, derive the causes from the PR's own test fixtures, not from intuition.

evidence: The 5f5eae4 rewrite of generate.ts says assistantOutput 'is exact, same as `unattributed` and `exactCost`'. But unattributed = exactCost - causedCost inherits estimator error, which the CallAttribution doc added in the same commit says outright ('One is the character estimator overshooting'). The PR merged at 08:21:47, before this round-1 review posted at 08:25:30, and the thread was never answered.
guidance_note: When one commit fixes two related findings, read the two rewritten docs against each other before pushing; here one said unattributed carries estimator error and the other called it exact.

narrative: Round 0 found four real findings: three overstated comments and a dropped Basis tag. One commit fixed all four correctly. That commit also rewrote the STILL-UNVERIFIED sentence and kept its false claim that unattributed is exact, which contradicted the doc the same commit added for F4. The agent merged before the round-1 review posted, so F5 shipped unaddressed.
guidance_observations: The PR merged before its final review round finished, so a valid S3 finding was never answered; merge should wait for the review triggered by the last fix push.
When fixes land in one combined commit, cross-read the docs it rewrites for contradictions between them.
